title: The Go SDK's response cache and request deduplication

prose.text: The SDK can cache GET responses and collapse identical GETs into one request. Providers that turn this on inherit its behavior on every read. {{zia-provider-enables-cache}}

checks.do: Whether a stale result after a write from the same client, within the cache lifetime, is a cached read rather than a server fault.

zia-provider-enables-cache.statement: The ZIA Terraform provider turns on the SDK's response cache for its OneAPI client, with a 10-minute entry lifetime. The provider's "idle timeout" setting is actually the cache's cleanup interval, so an expired entry can survive until the next cleanup.

quotes: zia.WithCacheTtl(10 * time.Minute), // Cache entries for 10 minutes
zia.WithCacheTti(8 * time.Minute),  // Idle timeout of 8 minutes
func NewCache(ttl, cleanWindow time.Duration, maxCacheSizeMB int) (Cache, error) {

waiters-ignore-cancellation.statement: When a GET for the same URL is already in flight, later identical GETs wait for it on a plain wait group, so a cancelled or timed-out caller stays blocked until the first request finishes.

quotes: existingIfr.wg.Wait() // Wait for the in-flight request to complete

owner-error-not-shared.statement: If the first in-flight GET fails, waiting callers do not receive its error: the error and response fields they check are never set, so each waiter sends the request again.
owner-error-not-shared.conditions: The reads are quoted. That nothing assigns the in-flight record's err, resp, or result was established by searching the file at v3.8.44 and HEAD; absence cannot be quoted.

quotes: // If no error but not cached, something went wrong - proceed with normal request

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK cache contract) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

two-owners-possible.statement: Claiming a URL as in flight is a separate check and store rather than one atomic step, so two GETs that miss the cache at the same moment can both send the request.

write-invalidates-but-inflight-get-repop.statement: A write clears the cached entries for its URL and parent collection before it is sent, and caching a GET response is unconditional. So a GET that started before the write took effect can store the pre-write response after the invalidation, and that response is then served until it expires.
write-invalidates-but-inflight-get-repop.conditions: Needs a GET to start before a write and finish after it. The code allows it; how often it happens depends on timing.

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK cache contract) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

parent-collection-invalidation.statement: A write also clears the parent collection's cached list. The SDK added this because a stale collection read after a child change broke the ZIA provider's rule reordering (SUP-3988).

quotes: // Also invalidate the parent collection endpoint so that list
// responses (e.g. /sslInspectionRules) are cleared when a child
// this, a GET on the collection is served stale from cache for
// up to the TTL after a child PUT/POST/DELETE, which breaks
// any client logic that mutates and immediately re-reads

prefix-invalidation-over-broad.statement: Invalidation matches cache keys by raw string prefix, and a write's parent key is its URL cut at the last `/`, so a create on a top-level collection such as `/zia/api/v1/firewallFilteringRules` clears every cached read under `/zia/api/v1`. The match only deletes entries, so the cost of the over-broad match is extra API reads.

quotes: // Check if there's an in-flight request for the same URL

cached-body-read-errors-ignored.statement: When serving from cache, an error reading the cached body is ignored: the caller gets whatever was read, and no error.
